class_id: a heading match that is really a prose cross-reference
feature: any extractor that locates a section of a filing by matching its heading text (scraper/src/services/peer-table-section.ts and every future document-section locator)
symptom: a document mentions a section by name inside a sentence - typically a footnote reading 'the peer set provided below under "Comparison with listed industry peers"' - and a matcher anchored on the phrase alone binds to that MENTION instead of the heading. The extractor then parses the wrong region: the notes above the table rather than the table. It does not crash and it does not warn; it returns a confident, empty or wrong result.
first_seen: 2026-09-11, item 8a. Twice, both mine, and the second is the instructive one. First I searched four RHPs for 'comparison with listed industry peers', got zero hits because the documents word it differently, and filed issue #565 claiming the table does not exist at all - reading zero hits as a fact about the document rather than about my pattern. Then, correcting that, I recorded Glasswall's heading AS 'Comparison with listed industry peers' - which is the text of its footnote's cross-reference, not its heading. Its real heading, twelve lines below, reads 'VI. Comparison of accounting ratios with listed industry peers'. The wrong wording was merged onto the build card in PR #579 before the locator's own tests caught it.
fix_prs: #587 - the locator requires the heading PHRASE TO START THE LINE after an optional section marker, so a mid-sentence mention cannot match. The card's wording corrected in the same PR.
detection_check: scraper/tests/unit/services/peer-table-section.test.ts - the case 'Glasswall: the heading is NOT the cross-reference twelve lines above it' asserts the located heading line comes AFTER the cross-reference line, on real committed fixture text; plus 'a prose mention inside a sentence is not a heading'. Mutation-checked with an assertion that the mutation applied: dropping the line-start requirement turns four cases red.
status: guarded for this locator only; any future section locator must re-establish the same property, since the guard lives in this locator's tests rather than in a shared rule
